GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for starring this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a Cloudflare tunnel domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to escpos-php library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend Sam mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!

It works with different parsing models to help users locate content that needs review. ## MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 **MiniCPM-OCR 1.0** (1.3B) is the first OCR-specific model in the MiniCPM-V/o family. It focuses on text-centric document understanding, covering text, tables, formulas, charts, seals, and structured information extraction.
